skill.name: code-reviewer
skill.description: Review code and pull requests with Python CLI scaffolds, checklist references, and quality guidance for common application stacks.

skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives from markdown headings, code fences, and setup examples. The real concern is that each Python script can write JSON output to an unconstrained user supplied path. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Unrestricted output file paths in Python scripts
remediation.suggestion: Validate --output paths, reject parent traversal or unsafe absolute paths, and warn before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: Command examples can be mistaken for automatic execution
remediation.suggestion: State that shell commands are examples for user approval, and remove deployment commands that are not required for review workflows.

content.value_statement: Code reviews often miss consistency, security, and maintainability issues across varied stacks. This skill provides review scripts, checklists, and structured guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Provides three Python CLI scripts for PR analysis, code quality checks, and review report generation.
Validates that the supplied target path exists before running a script.
Can print JSON results or save them through the --json and --output options.
Includes reference documents for review checklists, coding standards, and common antipatterns.
Lists review coverage for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, Swift, Kotlin, and common web stacks.
limitations: The included scripts are scaffolds and do not perform deep source analysis.
Automated fixes are described in documentation but are not implemented in the scripts.
Output file paths are not constrained, so users should choose safe destinations.
Reference documents contain generic guidance rather than framework-specific rules.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request before merge
use_cases.description: Use the PR analyzer and checklist guidance to structure findings before approving a change.

use_cases.title: Prepare team review standards
use_cases.description: Use the coding standards references to create shared expectations for readability, tests, and security.

use_cases.title: Create a lightweight review report
use_cases.description: Use the report generator scaffold to produce a simple status and findings summary for a target path.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a focused change set.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-reviewer skill to review this small change. Focus on correctness, readability, tests, and security issues.

prompt_templates.title: Check Pull Request Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the PR analyzer guidance to assess this pull request. Summarize blockers, non-blocking suggestions, and missing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Code Quality Across a Folder
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a project area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code quality checker workflow for this target folder. Report maintainability risks, performance concerns, and security observations.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Release Review Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the review report generator approach to prepare a release review. Include risk ranking, test gaps, ownership questions, and recommended next steps.

output_examples.input: Review a TypeScript pull request that changes authentication flow.
output: Summary: The change is understandable but needs stronger session handling tests.
Findings: Validate token expiry paths, add negative authorization tests, and document migration effects.
Recommendation: Do not merge until the authentication edge cases are covered.

output_examples.input: Assess a Python service folder for code quality concerns.
output: Summary: The folder is organized clearly, but error handling is inconsistent.
Findings: Normalize logging, add input validation near external boundaries, and reduce duplicated parsing logic.
Recommendation: Address the validation and logging items before broad rollout.

output_examples.input: Generate a review report for a release candidate.
output: Summary: Release risk is moderate because tests do not cover rollback paths.
Findings: Add deployment verification, define owner signoff, and confirm database migration reversibility.
Recommendation: Complete release checklist items before production deployment.

best_practices: Run scripts only against repositories and folders you intend to review.
Review generated findings manually before treating them as merge blockers.
Use safe output paths and avoid overwriting important project files.
anti_patterns: Do not use the scaffold scripts as a substitute for real test execution.
Do not run deployment commands from examples during a code review session.
Do not assume the reference documents cover every framework-specific rule.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically fix code?
faq.answer: No. The documentation mentions automated fixes, but the included scripts do not implement code changes.

faq.question: Can it review multiple programming languages?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for common stacks including TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Go, Swift, and Kotlin.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No evidence of network access was found in the reviewed files.

faq.question: Can it write files?
faq.answer: Yes. Each Python script can save JSON output when the --output option is provided.

faq.question: Is it suitable for security review?
faq.answer: It can guide security checks, but it does not replace dedicated security scanners or expert review.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
